Subject: Post-call recap + next steps (FinWave)

Thanks again for your time today, Alicia & Tom — good conversation and appreciate the transparency on production constraints and latency targets. Quick recap + proposed next steps: 

- Current ask: host ingest + retrieval Q&A at ~200ms p95 per request, mixed short/medium contexts (prompt ~150 tokens, response ~300 tokens).
- Primary concerns you raised: throughput cost, occasional hallucination on financial abbreviations, and auditability for model rollouts.

Proposed immediate follow-ups (what we'll deliver by EOD Thurs):
1) Share a recommended model shortlist with benchmark links and expected p95 on our Dedicated stack
2) A small eval set (we'll push a prompt set + expected scoring rubric) so you can run quick quality checks
3) A quantization trade-study summary (AWQ vs GPTQ vs FP8) focused on throughput/latency vs observed quality regressions

Internal: looping Connor and Ethan for ops/quantization notes; Rishi to track commercial/discount ask. Alicia/Tom — can you confirm the eval rubric (accuracy on entity extraction + concise financial reasoning) and whether you need strict token-level logging for compliance?

Thanks,
Marissa

Thanks Marissa — that looks great. Quick answers:
- Rubric: prioritize entity extraction accuracy (ticker/symbol, currency, date) then factual correctness for short reasoning. We'll use F1 for entities and a 0-2 scale for reasoning correctness.
- Logging: we need token-level request/response logs for audit (obfuscated PII ok).

Please include expected delta in model quality when using high-compression quantization (we care about any >2% drop in F1). If you can include a short example where AWQ/GPTQ/FP8 cause different outputs on one of the promptset examples that'd be helpful.

--

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Alicia Gomez <alicia.gomez@finwave.com>
Cc: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>, Ethan Park <ethan.park@redwood.com>, Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
Date: 2028-03-23T10:22:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: model shortlist + eval data + quantization summary

Hi Alicia — following up with the deliverables we discussed. High level notes below; full artifacts attached/linked.

1) Recommended model shortlist (for your latency & cost targets):
- Llama-3-13b-int8 (baseline): good tradeoff for moderate quality + low cost. Expected p95 ~230ms on Dedicated 1xA100-80GB with batching disabled; per-token cost mid.
- Mistral-Inference-7b-awq (AWQ profile): best throughput for same-class accuracy; p95 ~170ms but can show small entity regressions on highly compressed AWQ configs.
- Falcon-40b-gptq (GPTQ-conservative): strong reasoning quality, higher memory; p95 ~320ms unless aggressively quantized.

2) Eval artifacts: attached prod-qa-promptset.pdf (45 prompts), plus we exported the initial run results as finwave-eval-results.csv. Links: https://drive.google.com/finwave-evals/1a2b3c

3) Quantization trade-study summary (key takeaways):
- AWQ (aggressive int4/awq): +20-40% token throughput vs int8, p95 latency improvements 15-30% depending on model. Observed small drops in entity F1 on 4/45 prompts when using highest compression (int4 awq). Worst-case F1 delta: ~2.8% on a noisy ticker extraction example.
- GPTQ (per-layer quant): better preserved reasoning quality vs extreme AWQ configs; throughput gains smaller (~10-20%) but quality regressions typically <1%. Worthwhile if reasoning correctness is primary.
- FP8 (mixed float8 kernels): intermediate throughput gains, minimal quality impact on reasoning; requires runtime kernel support and increases inference memory slightly.

Attached are two short examples in the CSV where outputs diverge (rows 12 and 27). Example summary: for prompt #27 (ambiguous ticker shorthand), AWQ-int4 returned a generic fiscal statement causing entity mis-extraction, GPTQ-int8 preserved the ticker.

4) Recommended next steps (if you want to validate quickly):
- We can run a 48-hour eval on Dedicated using your promptset across the three profiles (Llama-3-int8 baseline, Mistral-AWQ, Falcon-GPTQ) and capture token-level audit logs. Estimated cost: ~USD 1,200 (we can offset as trial credit).
- If you'd like, Connor can propose an AWQ config that balances throughput and the specific F1 tolerances you set (e.g., keep F1 delta <2%).

Connor/Ethan — can you run a quick ops estimate for the 48-hour eval and share the expected p95 numbers for Dedicated v2? Rishi — can you prepare the trial credit note we mentioned for FinWave (target ~50% offset).

Thanks — attaching the CSV and promptset.

Best,
Marissa

Attachments: finwave-eval-results.csv, prod-qa-promptset.pdf

From: Connor O'Brien <connor.obrien@redwood.com>

Date: 2028-03-24T09:18:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: model shortlist + eval data + quantization summary

Quick ops note (48-hour eval estimate):
- Config: Dedicated v2 pool, 1xA100-80GB, single instance, no batching (to meet p95 targets) for parity across models.
- Expected p95 numbers (approx):
  * Mistral-Inference-7b-awq (AWQ-int4 optimized): 160-180ms p95
  * Llama-3-13b-int8: 220-250ms p95
  * Falcon-40b-gptq (GPTQ-int8): 300-340ms p95
- Storage & logging: token-level logs (obfuscated PII) will add ~15% to storage cost for the eval window.
- Risk notes: AWQ-int4 shows a small but measurable regression on ~5% of samples in our internal finance promptset; recommend running the eval and letting us threshold (we can automatically revert that request class to GPTQ if F1 drops >2%).

Alicia — if you give the green light we'll schedule the run tomorrow morning and share a live dashboard (latency/cost/quality) as we stream results.

Connor
